data.description:
`scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` exits 1 on current `origin/main`:

```
planning-corpus check: corpus=114 (want 113); missed=[]; mechanical_fp=[]; FAIL
```

Reproduced UNCHANGED on a pristine detached worktree at `origin/main` (with the tracker symlinked in), so this is not caused by ticket 1dd5's change: the flagged set is still exactly `ADJUDICATED_SUBSTANTIVE` (`missed=[]`, `mechanical_fp=[]`); only the corpus SIZE arm fails.

Root cause shape: the corpus is described in the module docstring as 'pinned and reproducible', but it is re-derived at run time from LIVE ticket state — the ancestors of `PLANNING_CORPUS_BOUNDARY` whose subject prefix resolves to a ticket whose CURRENT `ticket_type` is `bug` (`_resolve_bug_ticket` -> `_ticket_type`). Reclassifying any historical ticket to/from `bug`, or adding a ticket that changes short-prefix resolution, moves the count. `PLANNING_CORPUS_SIZE = 113` is therefore a constant asserted against a moving derivation.

Nothing in CI or the test suite runs this script, so the drift went unnoticed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `python scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py --check-planning-corpus` exits 0 on `origin/main`, OR the size assertion is replaced by one that does not depend on live ticket state (e.g. pin the 113 SHAs, not the count).
- [ ] The decision is recorded in the script's docstring so the 'pinned and reproducible' claim matches what the code does.
data.title: backtest --check-planning-corpus pin drifts: corpus=114, want 113
